thread: Tuesday 10/20 NBA Opening Day Game Thread!
text: I am really not a fan of these teams that construct their roster such that their star is heavily compensating for other players deficiencies. The Spurs are running out 3 non-shooting guards and another guard at PF and wondering why they have issues. I get why they are stuck (guys like Castle and Harper are still very young) but it's not optimal in any way. We saw the Knicks shut them down because they knew they could go under every time because the guards aren't shooting threats. Wemby has flaws but to reach some baseline level of offense he has to be parked at the 3pt line because none of the guards (where you usually get your shooting) can do it. None of them are great pnr creators for others (at least not yet). So it's "hey Wemby, I know we don't have anyone who can get you easy shots or space the floor for you or help with rim protection and rebounding so if you could cover all of that it would be great. Thanks" Wemby's game helps everyone else in the Spurs starting lineup but who is helping him? At some point the Spurs are going to need to invest in shooting, size, or both. Their guards have talent but the fit isn't good. I don't think this 3 guard thing is tenable long term if they really want to put the best team out on the floor. I'm not trying to absolve Wemby of his own flaws but the flaws that could cost the Spurs another title aren't Wemby related.

thread: Shams- Cason Wallace Extends w/ OKC 5 year $139 million
text: I'm fine with someone feeling OKC could use more secondary creators in the halfcourt. I disagree, but there are obviously teams with more in that category. I don't think we should over focus on the weaknesses though, when OKC won a title, and then went 7 games the conference finals with some bad injury luck. OKC doesn't have to have the best halfcourt offense to win a championship, because the guys they do have on the roster, with the strengths those guys have, help OKC win in a different way. OKC dominates the possession game by forcing turnovers at an elite rate, while rarely turning the ball over themselves. Their turnover generation gets them 22 points per game, so you can see why they're fine with prioritizing guys like Cason, Caruso, and J.Dub rather than giving up on some of them to upgrade the secondary halfcourt creation. There's multiple ways to win and obviously there's nothing wrong with how OKC does it. The nice thing about turnover generation is that it creates easy offense against good defenses. Opponents can try to mitigate turnovers, but it's something the defense has more influence on than the offense. Every team has strengths and weaknesses. I think sometimes we get lost when analysing really good teams when we point too hard at the weakness and pretend it's damning when it's just part of an equation that is still leading to big success overall. No team can have everything.
